speaks inside the baraita, 28b.2 (restated in the emended text at 28b.3)
anonymous redactorial voice of this sugya

props.gloss_en: synagogues -- one does not behave in them with frivolity
one does not eat in them
and one does not drink in them
and one does not adorn oneself in them
and one does not stroll in them
and one does not enter them in the sun because of the sun
or in the rain because of the rain
and one does not eulogize in them an individual's eulogy
but one reads [Scripture] in them
and one studies [mishna] in them
and one eulogizes in them a eulogy of the many
R' Yehuda: when [does this apply]? when they are inhabited
but in their ruin they are left alone and grass grows in them
and he should not pluck [the grass]
because of anguish
the baraita is lacking and teaches thus: and they sweep them and sprinkle them, so that grass does not grow in them
Rav Asi: the synagogues of Babylonia are made on condition
Rav Asi: and even so, one does not behave in them with frivolity
and what is it [the frivolity meant]? calculations
Rav Asi: a synagogue in which calculations are calculated -- they lodge the dead in it overnight
rather [Rav Asi means]: in the end they will lodge a met mitzva in it overnight

objections.gloss_en: עשבים מאן דכר שמייהו? -- the baraita said nothing of grass; how does R' Yehuda come to speak of it?

answered_by.gloss_en: חסורי מיחסרא והכי קתני: ומכבדין אותן ומרביצין אותן כדי שלא יעלו בהן עשבים -- the baraita had a clause about grass, to which R' Yehuda's אימתי responds (= p_mechabdin_umarbitzin)

objections.gloss_en: מלינין סלקא דעתך? לא סגי דלאו הכי? -- can it enter your mind that they lodge the dead there? is there no other way?

answered_by.gloss_en: אלא, לסוף שילינו בו מת מצוה -- rather: in the end they will lodge a met mitzva there (= p_sofo_met_mitzva; an explication, not a refutation -- header)
